title: Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (BC28): Use self-billed invoices
summary: Business Central 2026 wave 1 (BC28) introduces self-billed invoices, allowing buyers to generate invoices on behalf of suppliers under mutual agreement. This feature streamlines purchasing processes through automated layouts, dedicated number series, vendor configuration, and a specialized report layout that formats self-billed invoices in sales invoice style.
key_points: Buyers can now create invoices on behalf of vendors when a self-billing agreement is enabled via a new Boolean field on the Vendor Card
Purchase invoices for self-billing vendors are automatically marked as self-billed with restricted editable fields like Vendor Invoice No.
Vendors can be assigned dedicated number series for self-billed invoices to ensure correct document sequencing separate from posted purchase invoice numbers
A new report layout formats self-billed invoices in sales invoice style with buyer company information, vendor details, and VAT information

Danish localizations can automatically create Digital Vouchers during self-billing posting for compliance, and vendors with self-billing agreements cannot receive inbound e-documents for accounts payable

quotes.text: Self‑billing reduces operational friction by allowing buyers to generate invoices on behalf of suppliers under a mutual agreement.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core benefit of self-billing in reducing buyer-supplier coordination burden and improving invoice reliability.

quotes.text: All Purchase Invoices created for that vendor, whether from Purchase Orders or directly, are automatically marked as self‑billed.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that the system automates invoice classification once self-billing is configured, reducing manual steps.
